reforms.description: The federal government has refocused the National Research Council (NRC) on business-oriented research to better support innovation in the private sector.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: By aligning NRC's research focus with business needs, the reform aims to enhance the commercialization of research and foster innovation in the private sector.
reforms.status_evidence: The NRC has been refocused to support business-oriented research.
reforms.importance_rationale: This reform represents a significant shift in the NRC's focus, which could lead to improved collaboration between public research and private sector innovation.
reforms.source_quote: The government has refocused the NRC on business-oriented research.

reforms.description: The 2012 budget proposed to double funding to small and medium-sized businesses through the Industrial Research Assistance Program (IRAP), enhancing support for innovation.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Increasing funding to IRAP is expected to enhance the capacity of small and medium-sized enterprises to innovate and compete.
reforms.status_evidence: Funding to small and medium-sized businesses through IRAP is being doubled immediately.
reforms.importance_rationale: This funding increase is a significant enhancement of an existing program aimed at fostering innovation among SMEs.
reforms.source_quote: Funding to small and medium-sized businesses through IRAP is being doubled immediately.

reforms.description: The federal government has proposed to improve targeting of government support for business R&D by shifting funding from the SR&ED tax subsidies to direct grants, aiming to enhance the efficiency of R&D funding.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: By reallocating funds to direct grants, the reform aims to enhance the effectiveness of R&D investments, potentially leading to increased innovation and productivity.
reforms.status_evidence: The federal budget proposed significant changes to R&D funding targeting.
reforms.importance_rationale: This reform represents a significant shift in funding strategy aimed at improving the effectiveness of R&D support, which is crucial for fostering innovation.
reforms.source_quote: Further improve targeting of government support for business R&D by shifting funding at the margin away from the scientific research and experimental development (SR&ED) tax subsidies.

reforms.description: The government has announced plans to streamline regulatory approvals for major infrastructure projects, which is expected to enhance the efficiency of project implementation and support innovation in related sectors.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: By reducing regulatory burdens, the reform aims to facilitate faster project execution, which can lead to increased investment and innovation in infrastructure.
reforms.status_evidence: The recent federal budget proposes significant streamlining of regulatory approvals for major infrastructure projects.
reforms.importance_rationale: This initiative is significant as it aims to enhance the efficiency of infrastructure projects, which are critical for supporting broader economic growth and innovation.
reforms.source_quote: The recent federal budget, in fact, proposes significant streamlining of regulatory approvals for major infrastructure projects such as oil pipelines.

reforms.description: The federal government is enhancing the Business Immigration Program to attract experienced investors and innovative entrepreneurs, aiming to stimulate investment in Canadian growth companies.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Attracting skilled immigrants and entrepreneurs is expected to boost innovation and investment in Canadian firms, enhancing overall economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The federal government outlined that it will begin to target more active investment in Canadian growth companies and more innovative entrepreneurs under the Business Immigration Program.
reforms.importance_rationale: This reform is significant as it aims to enhance the entrepreneurial landscape in Canada by attracting skilled immigrants, which can lead to increased innovation and economic activity.
reforms.source_quote: The federal government outlined that it will begin to target more active investment in Canadian growth companies and more innovative entrepreneurs under the Business Immigration Program.

reforms.description: The Canadian government proposed to reduce the general SR&ED investment tax credit rate from 20% to 15% as part of the 2012 federal budget, aligning it with recent corporate income tax reductions.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: The reduction in the tax credit may discourage R&D investment by firms, particularly larger ones that rely on these credits for funding their research activities.
reforms.status_evidence: The 2012 federal budget proposed the reduction in the SR&ED tax credit rate.
reforms.importance_rationale: While the reform represents a significant change in the tax credit structure, it is not a complete overhaul of the innovation funding system in Canada.
reforms.source_quote: The 2012 federal budget proposes, as of 2014, a reduction in the general SR&ED investment tax credit rate from 20% to 15%.

reforms.description: The 2012 federal budget doubled the contributions of the Industrial Research Assistance Program (IRAP) to small and medium-sized businesses, enhancing support for R&D and innovative activities.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: By increasing funding for R&D and innovative activities, the reform aims to stimulate business innovation and enhance competitiveness.
reforms.status_evidence: The 2012 federal budget doubled the programme’s contributions to small and medium-sized businesses.
reforms.importance_rationale: The increase in funding for IRAP represents a significant enhancement of support for SMEs, which is crucial for fostering innovation.
reforms.source_quote: The 2012 federal budget doubled the programme’s contributions to small and medium-sized businesses.

reforms.description: The Jenkins report recommended using savings from streamlining the small-firm SR&ED to expand the Industrial Research Assistance Program (IRAP) and commercialisation vouchers, while consolidating smaller programmes into distinct product lines.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Expanding IRAP and commercialisation vouchers is expected to enhance support for innovation and R&D activities among small firms, thereby fostering economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The report's recommendations were acted upon to enhance the effectiveness of existing programmes.
reforms.importance_rationale: This reform represents a significant restructuring of funding mechanisms for innovation, aiming to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of public support for R&D.
reforms.source_quote: The Jenkins report...recommended using the savings from streamlining the small-firm SR&ED to expand IRAP and commercialisation vouchers.

reforms.description: The Jenkins panel report supported using public procurement to bolster innovation, particularly for SMEs, by framing procurement tenders in terms of needs to be met rather than detailed specifications.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: By encouraging innovative solutions through public procurement, the policy aims to stimulate market demand for new technologies and services, thus supporting economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The report's recommendations were adopted to enhance public procurement practices.
reforms.importance_rationale: This reform enhances existing procurement practices to better support innovation, particularly for small and medium enterprises.
reforms.source_quote: The Jenkins panel report supported using public procurement to bolster innovation, particularly for SMEs.

reforms.description: The 2012 federal budget allocated an additional CAD 500 million to support venture capital, including CAD 100 million through the BDC, aimed at enhancing the private VC and equity industry.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: This funding is expected to stimulate private investment in venture capital, thereby enhancing innovation and economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The federal budget made available an extra CAD 500 million in funding to VC support.
reforms.importance_rationale: This reform represents a significant increase in public investment in venture capital, which is crucial for fostering innovation and supporting the growth of the private equity market.
reforms.source_quote: The 2012 federal budget made available an extra CAD 500 million in funding to VC support, including CAD 100 million through the BDC.

reforms.description: The government has removed major tax barriers to private equity, facilitating a more favorable environment for venture capital investments.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: By eliminating tax barriers, the reform encourages private investment in venture capital, which can lead to increased innovation and economic activity.
reforms.status_evidence: The federal government has removed major tax barriers to private equity.
reforms.importance_rationale: This reform significantly alters the investment landscape for private equity, promoting a more dynamic venture capital market essential for innovation.
reforms.source_quote: The federal government has removed major tax barriers to private equity.

reforms.description: The government is attempting to stimulate academic-business collaborations and knowledge transfers through networks of excellence and incubators, aiming to reduce informational asymmetries and transaction costs that hinder collaboration.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Facilitates the transfer of knowledge and technology from academia to the market, enhancing innovation and productivity.
reforms.status_evidence: Governments are attempting to stimulate academic-business collaborations.
reforms.importance_rationale: This initiative represents a significant effort to enhance collaboration between academia and industry, which is crucial for fostering innovation.
reforms.source_quote: Governments are also attempting to stimulate academic-business collaborations and knowledge transfers through networks of excellence, incubators and the like.

reforms.description: The Competition Policy Review Panel suggested that Canada's tertiary education institutions could expedite the transfer of IP rights by moving to an 'innovator ownership' model, which would enhance commercialization of university research.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Encourages universities to commercialize research effectively, potentially leading to increased innovation and economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The Competition Policy Review Panel suggested that Canada’s tertiary education institutions could expedite the transfer of IP rights.
reforms.importance_rationale: This proposal aims to significantly improve the commercialization of university research, which is vital for enhancing innovation in Canada.
reforms.source_quote: The Competition Policy Review Panel suggested that Canada’s tertiary education institutions could expedite the transfer of IP rights by moving to an 'innovator ownership' model.

reforms.description: The federal government introduced the Repayment Assistance Plan (RAP) in 2009 to provide eligible candidates with more affordable monthly payments based on their family income and size, helping to alleviate the burden of student debt.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: By easing the financial burden of student debt, the RAP encourages higher education attainment, which can enhance the skills and productivity of the workforce.
reforms.status_evidence: The RAP was introduced to assist students with their loan repayments.
reforms.importance_rationale: The RAP represents a significant effort to improve financial support for students, particularly those from lower-income backgrounds, thereby enhancing access to education.
reforms.source_quote: The federal government introduced the Repayment Assistance Plan (RAP) in 2009... based on their family income and family size.

reforms.description: The Canada Learning Bond (CLB) was introduced to provide financial support to low-income families, aiming to improve access to post-secondary education for their children.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: By targeting financial support to low-income families, the CLB aims to increase educational attainment, which is essential for long-term economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The Canada Learning Bond targets low-income families to provide financial support.
reforms.importance_rationale: The CLB is a targeted initiative that addresses financial barriers to education for low-income families, thereby promoting equity in access to post-secondary education.
reforms.source_quote: The Canada Learning Bond (CLB) targets low-income families, which work to provide targeted support to individuals facing non-financial and financial barriers.

reforms.description: The 2011 federal budget announced that HRSDC would reallocate CAD60 million over three years to fund the development of 'digital skills' among youth and Aboriginal groups, and to promote enrolment in key disciplines such as STEM disciplines.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Enhances the skill set of the workforce, particularly in high-demand areas, which can lead to increased innovation and productivity.
reforms.status_evidence: The federal budget allocated funds for the development of digital skills.
reforms.importance_rationale: The initiative addresses a critical skills gap in the workforce, particularly in STEM fields, which is essential for fostering innovation.
reforms.source_quote: The 2011 federal budget announced that HRSDC would reallocate CAD60 million over three years to fund the development of 'digital skills' among youth and Aboriginal groups, and to promote enrolment in key disciplines such as STEM disciplines.

reforms.description: The Canada Foundation for Innovation (CFI) funds infrastructure costs for research projects in Canadian universities, colleges, research hospitals, and non-profit research institutions, providing up to 40% of funding with additional support from institutions and partners.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: By funding research infrastructure, the CFI enhances the capacity for research and innovation, which can lead to increased productivity and economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The CFI has been established and continues to fund research infrastructure.
reforms.importance_rationale: The CFI represents a significant investment in research infrastructure, crucial for enhancing Canada's research capacity and innovation ecosystem.
reforms.source_quote: The CFI funds infrastructure costs for research projects in Canadian universities, colleges, research hospitals and non-profit research institutions.

reforms.description: The Canada Research Chairs programme provides funding to outstanding researchers and emerging talents, enhancing the research capacity of Canadian universities.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: By attracting and retaining top researchers, the programme strengthens the research base, which can lead to innovation and economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The programme has been created and continues to provide funding to researchers.
reforms.importance_rationale: This programme is a major initiative to enhance research capacity in Canada, directly impacting the quality and quantity of research output.
reforms.source_quote: The Canada Research Chairs programme provides funding of CAD200000 annually for seven years to 1000 Tier-1 chairs selected for outstanding research contributions.

reforms.description: The Indirect Costs programme provides annual grants to universities and colleges to help fund a portion of indirect institutional costs of federally funded research projects.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: By covering indirect costs, the programme enables institutions to better support research activities, thereby enhancing overall research output and innovation.
reforms.status_evidence: The programme was introduced to address the indirect costs of research.
reforms.importance_rationale: While important, this programme is a targeted initiative rather than a structural overhaul of the research funding system.
reforms.source_quote: The Indirect Costs programme provides annual grants to universities and colleges to help fund a portion of indirect institutional costs of federally funded research projects.

reforms.description: The Centres of Excellence in Commercialisation and Research programme (CECR) invests in centres to advance research and assist the commercialisation of new technologies, products, and services.
reforms.package_name: Centres of Excellence in Commercialisation and Research programme
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: By facilitating the commercialisation of research, the CECR programme enhances the transfer of knowledge to the market, promoting innovation and economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The CECR programme was launched to advance research and assist commercialisation.
reforms.importance_rationale: This programme represents a significant investment in bridging the gap between research and market application, crucial for enhancing innovation.
reforms.source_quote: The Centres of Excellence in Commercialisation and Research programme (CECR) is investing CAD285 million over five years in centres to advance research and assist the commercialisation of new technologies.

reforms.description: The federal government announced funding and appointed an advisory panel to develop an international education strategy aimed at enhancing Canada's global competitiveness in higher education.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Enhancing international education can attract foreign students and improve the skills of domestic students, contributing to a more skilled workforce and innovation capacity.
reforms.status_evidence: The federal government announced funding and appointed an advisory panel to develop an international education strategy.
reforms.importance_rationale: The strategy aims to improve Canada's international education standing, which is significant for attracting talent and fostering innovation.
reforms.source_quote: In 2011, the federal government announced funding and appointed an advisory panel to develop an international education strategy.

reforms.description: Québec introduced 'performance commitments' that tie tuition and public funding increases to the attainment of specific target indicators for universities.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Linking funding to performance indicators can incentivize universities to improve educational outcomes, thereby enhancing the overall quality of education and innovation.
reforms.status_evidence: Québec has introduced 'performance commitments', which formally designate all tuition and public funding increases to universities between 2012-13 and 2016-17 to meet objectives based on the attainment of 13 target indicators.
reforms.importance_rationale: This initiative represents a significant shift in how funding is allocated, aiming to improve educational quality and institutional accountability.
reforms.source_quote: Québec has introduced 'performance commitments', which formally designate all tuition and public funding increases to universities between 2012-13 and 2016-17 to meet objectives based on the attainment of 13 target indicators.

reforms.description: The Canadian government aims to boost innovation by sharpening incentives and raising performance in business R&D, suggesting a unification of the tax subsidy rate for small domestic firms at the lower large firm rate to encourage scale adoption of innovations.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: By unifying tax subsidies, firms are incentivized to scale up, which can lead to increased R&D investment and innovation.
reforms.status_evidence: The government has indicated a focus on improving business innovation and productivity growth.
reforms.importance_rationale: This reform represents a significant adjustment in the tax subsidy framework aimed at enhancing business R&D, which is crucial for improving innovation outcomes.
reforms.source_quote: Government support to R&D should focus more on sharpening incentives and raising performance; the higher current tax subsidy rate for small domestic firms should be unified at the lower large firm rate to encourage firms to attain the scale needed to adopt innovations.

reforms.description: The Canadian government emphasizes the need for improvements in tertiary education to support a knowledge-driven economy, focusing on increasing participation and equity of access.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Enhancing the quality and accessibility of tertiary education will help build a skilled workforce, which is essential for driving innovation and productivity.
reforms.status_evidence: Efforts should be increased to recruit foreign tertiary students and integrate them into the workforce upon graduation.
reforms.importance_rationale: This initiative is significant as it addresses the critical need for a skilled workforce in a knowledge-driven economy, impacting long-term economic growth.
reforms.source_quote: Further improving equity of access by reducing non-financial barriers and increasing targeted need-based financial assistance is a priority.

reforms.description: The Canadian government is focusing on improving the policy framework for innovation, particularly by strengthening the role of the tertiary education sector to enhance business innovation.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Enhancing the skills of the workforce and improving the performance of educational institutions can lead to increased innovation and productivity.
reforms.status_evidence: The overarching theme of this Survey is improving the policy framework for innovation.
reforms.importance_rationale: This reform represents a significant shift in policy focus towards innovation, aiming to enhance the capabilities of the tertiary education sector, which is crucial for long-term economic growth.
reforms.source_quote: The overarching theme of this Survey is improving the policy framework for innovation, including in particular by strengthening the role of the tertiary education sector.

reforms.description: The federal government has committed to reconfiguring the National Research Council (NRC) to focus more on demand-driven applied research that better serves the needs of businesses, addressing the commercialisation gap between academic and applied research.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: By aligning research efforts with business needs, this reform is expected to enhance innovation and productivity in the private sector.
reforms.status_evidence: The federal government has committed to carrying it further in its new budget.
reforms.importance_rationale: This reform represents a significant shift in the focus of a major public research institution, aiming to bridge the gap between academic research and business innovation.
reforms.source_quote: The Jenkins report for the federal government recommended that the National Research Council (NRC) – which governs the main public research institutes – be reconfigured to be more focused on demand-driven applied research better able to serve the needs of business.

reforms.description: The federal government has announced a study of contingency fees charged by tax preparers for the SR&ED tax incentive program, which is designed to support R&D activities in Canada.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: By examining and potentially reducing compliance costs, this reform could enhance the effectiveness of the SR&ED program, encouraging more firms to engage in R&D.
reforms.status_evidence: The 2012 budget announced a study of contingency fees charged by tax preparers.
reforms.importance_rationale: This reform addresses a significant issue within the SR&ED program, which is crucial for encouraging R&D investment among Canadian firms.
reforms.source_quote: The 2012 budget announced a study of contingency fees charged by tax preparers.
